column1: # Reviewed function-level semantic ground truth for EqBench Neq samples (Issue #104).
# Consumed by scripts/eqbench/function_diff_manifest.py.  The runner benchmark
# gate treats "CONFIRMED_NOT_EQ && checker EQUIVALENT" and
# "CONFIRMED_EQ && checker NOT_EQ" as hard violations (runner exit 1).
# The checker never reads this file.
# What an entry means (the gate is only as trustworthy as these rules):
#   CONFIRMED_NOT_EQ  a concrete input on which old and new observably differ,
#                     confirmed by a human from the source and by independent
#                     execution (not "the source changed", not "the checker
#                     said NOT_EQ").  Record the input and both outputs.
#   CONFIRMED_EQ      an algebraic / structural argument that the two
#                     definitions compute the same observable result for
#                     every input, plus independent execution probes.  A few
#                     agreeing samples alone are not enough.
# Entries apply to every runner pair (all ISAs, compilers, optimisation
# levels) of the (sample, function): the evidence must not depend on the
# architecture, type widths, floating-point environment or on how the
# compiler resolves undefined behaviour (e.g. a source-level algebraic
# argument that relies on signed-overflow wraparound does not justify
# CONFIRMED_EQ: -O2/-O3 may compile the two definitions differently).  Add a
# scope column before registering anything architecture-specific.
# An entry that resolves to no function of the benchmark tree makes the
# manifest build (and so the runner) fail closed.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   sample     Neq sample identity as the runner names it, e.g. REVE/triangularMod/Neq/newV-oldV
#   function   function name
#   verdict    CONFIRMED_NOT_EQ | CONFIRMED_EQ
#   evidence   how the verdict was confirmed (input, outputs, argument)
